grammar.title: Passive voice untuk laporan dan data
grammar.explanation: Dalam laporan, yang penting biasanya hasil atau datanya, bukan siapa pelakunya. Pakai be + V3 (was collected, have been tested, will be shared). Pastikan kata kerjanya bentuk ketiga.
examples: The feature was used by 40% of users.
Three options have been tested so far.
The results will be shared next week.

common_mistake.wrong: The survey was send to 500 users.
common_mistake.right: The survey was sent to 500 users.

grammar.title: Second conditional untuk usulan
grammar.explanation: Untuk membayangkan hasil sebuah usulan, pakai If + past simple, lalu would + V1. Jangan pakai 'would' di bagian 'if'. Bentuk ini terdengar lebih sopan dan hati-hati daripada 'will'.
examples: If we simplified the sign-up form, more people would finish it.
What would happen if we removed the free plan?
If I were you, I'd start with a small test.

common_mistake.wrong: If we would add a dark mode, users would like it.
common_mistake.right: If we added a dark mode, users would like it.

reading.title: Why most product pitches fail
reading.text: Most product pitches fail for a simple reason: they describe a solution before anyone agrees there is a problem. Decision-makers hear dozens of ideas every month, and they are naturally sceptical. A strong pitch starts with evidence that the problem is real and costly, such as support tickets, churn figures, or short clips from user interviews. Only then is the solution introduced, ideally as a small experiment rather than a large project. Experienced product managers also address objections before they are raised. If a feature might slow down the app, they say so, and explain how the risk would be measured. Finally, the best pitches end with a clear request: a budget, two engineers for a sprint, or simply permission to run a test. A pitch without a specific ask is just a presentation.

questions.q: According to the text, why do most pitches fail?
options: They present a solution before proving the problem

questions.q: How should the solution ideally be introduced?
What does the writer mean by 'a specific ask'?
options: A clear request, such as a budget or people

writing.prompt: Tulis email proposal ke kepala produk (Ms Patel). Usulkan satu fitur baru untuk aplikasimu. Jelaskan masalahnya dengan data, solusimu, risiko atau trade-off-nya, lalu tutup dengan permintaan yang spesifik.
checklist: Masalah dijelaskan dengan angka atau bukti
Minimal satu kalimat passive voice (… were analysed / … has been consulted)
Ada second conditional (If we …, we would …)
Ditutup dengan permintaan spesifik (orang, waktu, atau anggaran)
useful_phrases: Over the last three months, ... were analysed.
Could we have ... to run a two-week test?
writing.model_answer:
Subject: Proposal: one-tap sign-in for returning users

Hi Ms Patel,

I'd like to propose a small experiment to reduce drop-off at sign-in.

Over the last three months, 18,000 login attempts were analysed, and we found that 27% of returning users abandon the app at the password screen. Most of them are on mobile, where typing long passwords is frustrating. Support tickets tell the same story: password resets are now our most common request.

My suggestion is to add one-tap sign-in with a magic link sent by email. If we offered this option to returning users, I estimate that we would recover at least a third of those lost sessions. To put it simply, fewer people would give up before they even see their dashboard.

The main trade-off is security. Email links can be forwarded, so each link would expire after ten minutes and could only be used once. The legal team has already been consulted, and they have not raised any concerns so far.

Could we have two engineers for one sprint? We would release the feature to 10% of users, compare the results with the current flow, and share a short report before deciding whether to scale it up.

Best regards,
Bagus

speaking.prompt: Gaya IELTS Speaking Part 3: 'Do you think technology companies collect too much data about their users?' Jawab dengan pendapat, alasan, dan contoh (5 sampai 6 kalimat).
speaking.sample_answer: To some extent, yes. Many apps collect far more information than they actually need, and most users never read the privacy policy. For example, a simple flashlight app shouldn't need access to your contacts. On the other hand, some data is genuinely useful, because it helps companies fix bugs and improve their products. I think the real problem is transparency rather than the data itself. If companies explained clearly what they collected and why, people would trust them much more.

n1.them: I've read your proposal. Honestly, I'm not convinced we need another feature right now.
hints: akui kekhawatirannya: I understand your concern

fallback.feedback: Contoh: "I understand your concern. Could I explain why we think it's urgent?"

n2.them: Go on. What's the actual problem you're trying to solve?
hints: masalah + angka: Almost half of new users ...

fallback.feedback: Contoh: "Almost half of new users drop out during sign-up. The data was collected over three months."

n3.them: Fine, but how much is this going to cost us?
hints: perkiraan biaya: It would take two engineers for ...

fallback.feedback: Contoh: "It would only take two engineers for one sprint, because we'd start with a small test."

n4.them: And what if it doesn't work?
hints: second conditional: If it didn't work, we would ...

fallback.feedback: Contoh: "If it didn't work, we would simply roll it back. We'd measure the results after two weeks."

n5.them: Hmm. I suppose the benefits might outweigh the costs. What exactly do you need from me?
hints: permintaan spesifik: Could we have approval for ...?

fallback.feedback: Contoh: "Could we have approval for a two-week test with 10% of users?"

end.them: All right. Send me a one-page summary and I'll approve the test this week.
